sub_graphs.title: Electra: Weak Subjectivity Period Calculation
sub_graphs.description: Models the computation of the weak subjectivity period based on total active balance and churn limit

nodes.label: Beacon State Loaded
nodes.description: A beacon state has been loaded for weak subjectivity period computation

nodes.label: Compute Total Active Balance
nodes.description: Sum all active validator effective balances to get total active balance (t)

nodes.label: Compute Balance Churn Limit
nodes.description: Calculate the maximum validator set churn per epoch (delta), accounting for EIP-7251 increased max effective balances

nodes.label: Weak Subjectivity Period Known
nodes.description: The weak subjectivity period in epochs has been computed for this state

sub_graphs.title: Electra: Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint Validation
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation of a node's chain against its weak subjectivity checkpoint

nodes.label: Node Syncing with WS Checkpoint
nodes.description: Node has a weak subjectivity checkpoint (ws_state, ws_checkpoint) and is syncing the chain

nodes.label: Validate Checkpoint Block Root
nodes.description: Assert that the block root at the checkpoint epoch matches the ws_checkpoint root

nodes.label: Validate Checkpoint Epoch
nodes.description: Assert that the state epoch matches the ws_checkpoint epoch

nodes.label: Within Weak Subjectivity Period
nodes.description: Node is within the safe weak subjectivity window, chain history is trustworthy

nodes.label: Outside Weak Subjectivity Period
nodes.description: Node has exceeded the weak subjectivity period; chain history may not be safe

nodes.label: Checkpoint Validation Failed
nodes.description: The ws_checkpoint does not match the chain state, indicating a potential fork or attack

external_entities.name: Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint Provider
external_entities.description: Trusted external source providing the ws_state and ws_checkpoint (e.g., community consensus, checkpoint sync service)

sub_graphs.title: Electra: Long-Range Attack Protection Boundary
sub_graphs.description: Models the security boundary where weak subjectivity protects against long-range attacks

nodes.label: Node Online and Tracking Chain
nodes.description: Node is online, has a valid WS checkpoint, and is tracking the canonical chain

nodes.label: Node Offline Beyond WS Period
nodes.description: Node was offline longer than the weak subjectivity period and needs a fresh checkpoint

nodes.label: Receive Conflicting Chain from Peer
nodes.description: Node receives a chain from a peer that conflicts with its WS checkpoint

nodes.label: Long-Range Attack Rejected
nodes.description: Conflicting chain rejected because it disagrees with the WS checkpoint within the WS period

nodes.label: Node Needs Fresh WS Checkpoint
nodes.description: Node must obtain a new trusted WS checkpoint before safely resuming sync

edges.label: Chain conflicts with valid WS checkpoint
WS period exceeded, cannot trust stored state

external_entities.name: Long-Range Attacker
external_entities.description: Adversary presenting a conflicting chain history forked from an old finalized checkpoint

ambiguities.text: Clients may choose to validate the input state against the input Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume all conforming clients MUST validate the checkpoint. The 'may choose' language is interpreted as implementation flexibility in how validation is triggered, not whether it happens. This is an assumption.

ambiguities.text: No specification of what a node should do when it detects it is outside the weak subjectivity period
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the node should halt syncing and require operator intervention to provide a fresh WS checkpoint. This is an assumption.

implicit_assumptions.description: The weak subjectivity checkpoint provider is honest and provides a checkpoint from the canonical chain
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A malicious checkpoint provider could direct the node onto an attacker-controlled fork from the start

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot corrupt more than 1/3 of the validator set within the weak subjectivity period
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attacker could finalize conflicting checkpoints within the WS period, defeating the protection mechanism

implicit_assumptions.description: The SAFETY_DECAY constant of 10 provides sufficient margin against real-world validator churn rates
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: WS period could be too short, causing nodes to fall outside the safe window during normal operation
